characters.name: Kang the Conqueror
characters.description: A time-traveling conqueror with vast powers and technological supremacy, Kang has amassed an empire with a citizenry of millions, and cut a swath of terror through the ages. A strong contender for the title ofArch-Enemyof the Avengers as a whole, with Ultron being the only real challenger to that claim. In addition, several alternate versions of Kang have appeared throughout Marvel's titles over the years, including his respective future and past heroic selves, Immortus and Iron Lad. Kang first appeared inThe Avengers#8 (September, 1964), and was created by writerStan Leeand artistJack Kirby. Rama-Tut first appeared earlier inFantastic Four#19 (October, 1963). Immortus first appeared inAvengers#10 (November, 1964), while Iron Lad first appeared inYoung Avengers#1 (April, 2005). Kang has made a cameo inX-Men: The Animated Seriesepisode "Beyond Good and Evil", after appearing incognito as aCloudcuckoolanderfor several episodes. Kangmade his cinematic debut, portrayed byJonathan Majors, in theMarvel Cinematic UniversefilmAnt-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania. Two alternate versions of the character, He Who Remains and Victor Timely, appeared inLoki. Though Kang was set to be the newArc Villainof the MCU in the vein of Thanos for the Infinity Saga, despite the actor's praised performances and the positive reception toLoki, the mixed-to-negative reception ofQuantumaniaand Majors getting convicted of assault resulted inThe Kang Dynastybecoming anAborted Arc. Not to be confused with theSimpsonscharacter of the same name.

characters.name: Rama-Tut
characters.description: The first supervillain identity that Nathan Richards ever assumed. After studying the history of the Heroic Age of modern day Earth-616, Richards discovered a fully functional replica of a time platform believed to have been invented by Doctor Doom, and fashioned it into aTARDIS-like timeship resembling a sphinx. Traveling back to Egypt in the year 2960 BCE, Richards easily took over the land thanks to his superior technology, calling himself Rama-Tut and crowning himself Pharaoh. After learning of the existence of a powerful young mutant namedEn Sabah Nur, Rama-Tut seeks to claim him as his heir. Encountering the Fantastic Four andDoctor Strangeon their own time traveling adventures, Rama-Tut is eventually forced to flee back to the future and adopt the Kang persona, but some future incarnations have him resuming the Rama-Tut identity as a form of retirement. And Now You Must Marry Me: Tried to make Sue Storm marry him in his first appearance, via aHypno Ray. Been There, Shaped History: That famous Sphinx? His time-machine, left where he crashed it. In fact, most of the tech is still in there. The Caligula: Downplayed, but he is a despotic ruler who encourages his subjects to revere him as a god, and has several monuments built to reflect this. He is at his worst in his early reign, where this is all new to him and he'sDrunk with Power. The older, "retired" versions of him have mellowed with age. Evil Mentor: To Apocalypse. Itwent horribly right.

characters.name: Scarlet Centurion
characters.description: After Rama-Tut was ousted from his position as Pharaoh by the Fantastic Four, he attempted to return to his own time, but was caught in a temporal storm and crash landed in the modern era of Earth-616. A chance encounter with Doctor Doom prompted him to abandon the Rama-Tut identity and create a new supervillain persona similar to Doom's. He travels back in time to visit the founding Avengers lineup of Iron Man, Ant-Man, Thor, Wasp, and the Hulk, right before Hulk leaves the team, offering to share his knowledge of the future to help them bring about a golden era of peace. This creates a divergent reality: Earth-689. The Scarlet Centurion then pits the Earth-689 founders against the current Earth-616 Avengers. After his defeat, the Centurion again attempts to return to his own time, but ends up in the 40th Century, where he reinvents himself again, taking on the Kang identity. A divergent version of him went on to torment the Squadron Supreme of Earth-712.

characters.name: Immortus
characters.description: The supposed final incarnation of Nathaniel Richards. After several adventures as anEvil Overlord, Kang eventually becomeshumbled and disillusioned by his failures as a conqueror. Retiring from supervillainy, he initially resumes the identity of Rama-Tut and attempts to rule Egypt as a wiser, more benevolent ruler, but ultimately decides to spend his twilight years in Limbo, a pocket dimension that exists outside of the normal space/time continuum. However, theTime Keepershad other ideas. They tracked Richards down andmade him a proposition: Immortality in exchange for serving as the guardian for an 80 millennia span of the space-time continuum. Now calling himselfImmortus, he seeks to repair the damage his earlier selves have done to the time stream. Valuing order over chaos, Immortus alternately helps and hinders the Avengers as he maneuvers through the timestream, intent on preventing temporal paradoxes before they begin. The Ageless: Benefits of being a time-traveler working for the Time Keepers, he ismucholder than he looks, and he wasn't a spring chicken before he was given the job. Almighty Janitor: He's often calledCustodianof the Timestream. And inthe 90s X-Men animated series, he even disguises himself as a janitor named Bender (no, not that one).Kang:He calls himself the Master of Time! "Gardener of Time" is more truthful! He prunes away the chronal branches deemed byothersto be dangerous, reducing reality to a bloodless meadow! Army of The Ages: He's a step up from Kang in that he can summon one without techthanks to his powers, but hestillloves using these. Can't Kill You, Still Need You: Much as he'd like to get rid of Kang, just as Kang wants to kill him, he can't, because there has to be a Kang to become him. Of course, you'd be amazed what someone can live through...

characters.name: Iron Lad
characters.description: A 16-year-old Nathaniel Richards whose path diverges when his future self saves him from an assassination attempt. Hoping to spare him painful moments and accelerate his transformation to Kang (under more favorable circumstances), Kang shows the boy his (future) history and provides him with a suit of neurokinetic armour that responds to his subconscious thoughts. However, Young Nate is horrified by what he sees and becomes determined to prevent his destiny as a supervillain by any means necessary. Discovering that his armour had time travel capabilities, Nate travels back to modern day Earth-616 and attempts to contact the Avengers. However, by the time he arrives,the team had been disbanded. Altering his armor into a likeness of Iron Man's armor, Nate adopted the heroic persona ofIron Ladand used an Avengers Fail-Safe Program to createa new version of the team. Unfortunately, Iron Lad's conflict with Kang eventually created a temporal paradox that threatened to unravel the space-time continuum, forcing him to return to the future and embrace his supervillainous destiny. However it was later revealed that he continued to try and escape his fate, and tragedy would put him on the path to become Kid Immortus.

characters.name: Kid Immortus
characters.description: Full of grief from the death of Cassie Lang, who he had developed feelings for, Iron Lad escaped into the timestream with the goal of being better than his future selves. Calling himself Kid Immortus, he starts researching his destiny while also coming into conflict with Doctor Doom due to the manipulations of an alternate timeline Valeria Richards. All for Nothing: He decided to embrace his destiny to try and save Cassie Lang, only for her to be resurrected anyway by someone else. Fallen Hero: Not that long ago in his personal timeline he was Iron Lad, a wannabe hero trying to change his fate. Now he's Kid Immortus, having not only embraced his destiny but attempting to prove he was better than his future selves. Same Character, But Different: He's essentially the same version as Iron Lad.

characters.name: Mister Gryphon
characters.description: As a consequence of a glitch in the timestream, Kang the Conqueror was split apart into different versions of himself. One of these versions became trapped in the early 21st century, held back by some kind of "firewall of time." Unwilling to wait for two thousand years to catch up with his original era, this Nathaniel Richards decided to create his own dynasty in this time period. Under the alias of "Mister Gryphon," Kang became a businessman and the CEO of Qeng Enterprises. He additionally enlisted the help of several villains to make his empire grow. Corrupt Corporate Executive: His guise in the modern day. Trapped in the Past: Thanks to a "firewall of time", Kang got trapped in the here-and-now. Unwilling to wait it out and unable to get around the timewall (and with no future version of himself apparently able to help), he's stuck and tetchy.

characters.name: Doctor Doom
characters.description: Costume Copycat: He's a Kang who, for whatever reason, has decided to dress like Doctor Doom.

characters.name: Myrddin
characters.description: Red Is Heroic: Subverted. Despite leading a team of heroes, and fighting against Kang, his goals remain as malicious as most other versions of the character. Religious and Mythological Theme Naming: He's named after Myrddin Wyllt, the inspiration forMerlin.

characters.name: Ravonna Renslayer
characters.description: A time-traveling princess, conqueror, and assassin, Princess Ravonna has gone by many names: Terminatrix, Temptress, Revelation, and Nebula, and has battled the Avengers and the Fantastic Four. But mainly her beef is with Kang the Conqueror, who often desires her to be his bride... whether she wants to be or not. Alliterative Name:RavonnaRenslayer. Anguished Declaration of Love: Gives one as she jumps in front of a shot meant for Kang. Arc Villain: ForAvengersissues 291-297, andFantastic Four337-341, which followed on from it. Body Surf: Nebula-Ravonna wound up hopping into Johnny Storm's body for a while. When Sue noticed something was up, she hopped into Sue instead.

characters.name: Marcus Kang
characters.description: Marcus Kang is the son of the time-travelling world conqueror known as Kang. Abhorrent Admirer: Not because of anything personality wise, mind. He's actually an alright person, world-conquering aside. It's just that he looks exactly identical to Marcus Immortus, with whom Carol Danvers has an extremely unpleasant history. For what it's worth, he finds the actions of his "alternate counterpart" to be utterly abhorrent. Amazon Chaser: Falls in love with Carol Danvers the minute he sees her. He's far more respectful of her feelings and agency than theotherMarcus, butthat's not exactly a high bar to clear. Even Evil Has Standards: He's not exactly thrilled to learn what an "alternate" version of himself did to Carol Danvers, and expresses his sympathies when he learns of her trauma over the whole affair. Inadequate Inheritor: Notice that his name is Marcus the twenty-third? Kang created twenty-two other Marcii before him, and for one reason or another they all fell short of Kang's idea of a suitable heir. So he killed them. At the end ofKang War, Marcus discovers this. And then dad kills him for the same reason.

characters.name: Growing Man
characters.description: The Growing Man is a stimuloid who serves Kang the Conqueror. Do Androids Dream?: Despite being robots, the Growing Man occasionally show signs of personality. Energy Absorption: Any attack against the Growing Man is absorbed, and causes it to grow. However, there are limits to its ability; Hercules was once able to hit a Growing Man hard enough to overload it and render it essentially unconscious. In Working Order: The Growing Man can lie buried for millions of years and boot up again no problem. Killer Robot: A "stimuloid" built to fight Kang's enemies. Exactly what makes a stimuloid different from Marvel's other types of robots is unclear.

characters.name: Anachronauts
characters.description: A group of warriors from across time who were defeated by Kang and swore undying loyalty to him. Badass Crew: In theory, at any rate. A Day in the Limelight:Avengersannual #22 has a back-up story about them getting up to stuff while Kang's away involving travelling to Camelot and fighting the Incinerators. Dropped a Bridge on Him: They are all killed off-screen by Immortus duringAvengers: Forever, and their remains crushed along with the ruins of Chronopolis into the Forever Crystal. Kid from the Future: Apocryphus is Sersei's kid from an alternate timeline.
